# PR-002 Supplier Onboarding SOP

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure describes how Meridian Supply Co. qualifies a new supplier before it is trusted with regular purchase orders, and how it moves from first contact to the Approved Supplier List (ASL).

### 1.2 Scope
It applies to every new supplier of goods or services for resale or operations. Existing suppliers that change legal entity or ownership are onboarded again.

## 2. Required Documents

### 2.1 Onboarding checklist
Procurement collects the following before any PO is issued.

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Tax form | Completed W-9 |
| Insurance | Certificate showing $2M general liability cover |
| Quality | Completed quality questionnaire |
| Financial | Credit check run by Finance |

### 2.2 Insurance certificate
The certificate names Meridian Supply Co. as certificate holder, is in date and shows general liability cover of at least $2M per occurrence. Procurement diarises the expiry date and requests a renewed certificate 30 days before it lapses.

### 2.3 Quality questionnaire
The questionnaire covers the supplier's quality system, lot traceability, packaging standards and corrective action process. Quality reviews it and records a pass, a conditional pass or a fail. A fail stops onboarding.

### 2.4 Credit check
Finance runs the credit check and records the result and recommended payment terms. A poor result may lead to prepayment or a reduced credit limit.

## 3. Provisional Status

### 3.1 90-day provisional status
A supplier that has passed the checklist is set up as provisional. Provisional status lasts 90 days. During this period POs are limited to low-risk items and each delivery is inspected in full on receipt under WH-001.

### 3.2 Review at 90 days
At day 90 Procurement and Quality review the supplier's delivery, quality and invoice performance. A supplier with no open nonconformance reports and on-time delivery at target is moved to the Approved Supplier List.

### 3.3 Extension or rejection
A supplier that does not meet the standard has its provisional period extended once by 90 days or is rejected.

## 4. Approved Supplier List

### 4.1 Maintaining the ASL
The ASL is held by Procurement. Each entry shows the approval date, product categories, insurance expiry and quality status. Quality performance is monitored under QA-001.

### 4.2 Removal
A supplier is removed from the ASL for expired insurance that is not renewed, sustained poor quality, financial failure or breach of the supplier code of conduct.

## 5. Responsibilities

### 5.1 Procurement
Procurement runs the process, keeps the evidence and updates the ASL.

### 5.2 Quality and Finance
Quality owns the questionnaire decision. Finance owns the credit check and payment terms, which are normally net 45 as described in FIN-001.

### 5.3 Supplier code of conduct
Every supplier signs the Meridian supplier code of conduct during onboarding. It covers lawful labour practice, safe working conditions, anti-bribery and the handling of confidential information. A signed copy is stored with the supplier record.

### 5.4 Records and renewal
The onboarding file holds the documents listed in section 2.1, the questionnaire decision and the date provisional status started and ended. Approved suppliers are re-assessed every two years, or earlier if there is a change in ownership, location or product range.

### 5.5 Urgent requirements
If a requirement cannot wait for the full process, the Procurement Manager may approve a single trial order to a supplier that has not yet completed onboarding. The order is inspected in full and the checklist must be completed before any further order is placed.
